items.title: 川普擬禁美企海外建資料中心！微軟、Google在台布局添變數
items.title_en: Trump Plans to Ban U.S. Companies from Building Overseas Data Centers, Adding Uncertainty to Microsoft and Google's Taiwan Plans
paras: 美國總統川普週五 (20 日) 表示，不會允許美國企業在海外興建資料中心，並揚言對不配合的公司課徵「巨額稅負」，要求企業將投資留在美國。市場分析，這項構想勢必為美商在台資料中心的後續布局增添政策變數。
不過，川普坦言尚未與幕僚討論，相關限制是否涵蓋台灣、既有工程及合作開發模式，仍待釐清。
川普週五在白宮記者會上表示：「我們不會允許我們的企業在國外興建資料中心。我們不會讓這種事情發生。」
他將資料中心投資與過去晶片產業外移相提並論，認為美國曾允許晶片及其他產業移往海外，對國家造成重大傷害。
「他們讓晶片和其他各種東西發生這種情況，這對我們國家極具破壞性。那就是我們開始落後的時候。」川普說。
不過，他隨即補充：「這是個最新消息，但我甚至還沒跟我的幕僚說過。」顯示這項限制海外資料中心投資的構想，尚待政府進一步說明如何執行。
川普表示，若美國企業仍赴海外興建資料中心，將面臨「巨額稅負」。
他還警告，若任由這些資料中心落腳其他國家，「中國會把它們全部拿走」，但未進一步解釋具體所指。
川普這項構想勢必為美商在台資料中心的後續布局增添政策變數
對台灣而言，微軟 (MSFT-US) 的資料中心擴建是值得關注的布局。
台灣微軟總經理卞志祥今年 9 月表示，因應未來兩至三年 AI 算力需求持續高於供給，微軟正積極在台擴建資料中心，整體架構將由原先兩座擴充為四座。
若美方後續措施涵蓋海外新增設施或擴建投資，相關建置與資金配置可能面臨重新評估。
Google 母公司 Alphabet (GOOGL-US) 在台南、雲林的潛在資料中心規畫，也可能面臨新的政策不確定性。
此外，亞馬遜 (AMZN-US) 旗下 AWS 已於 2025 年 6 月啟用亞太 (台北) 區域，並承諾長期在台投資超過 50 億美元，用於資料中心建設、連網、營運與維護。
因此，後續政策是否僅限制新建案，或連既有區域的擴充投資也納入，將影響其在台布局的評估。
同樣值得注意的是，政策如何認定企業角色？例如輝達 (NVDA-US) 參與鴻海在台 AI 超級運算中心建置，但由鴻海體系主導開發，與美商自行投資興建的模式不同。
美方是否將設備供應、技術合作、租用機房或採購算力納入限制，川普此次談話均未交代，目前無法據此判定相關合作案受限。
為推動投資留在國內，川普週四強調，美國仍有許多地區願意接納資料中心，企業不必因部分地方不歡迎而轉向海外。
「我們希望他們在這裡興建。如果他們不去德州、不去加州，那就去西維吉尼亞州。」他說，「我們有很多地方非常想要它們，而且都是很棒的地方。」
川普也以資料中心密集的維吉尼亞州勞登郡 (Loudoun County) 為例，形容當地「賺了這麼多錢，多到不知道該怎麼用」，呼籲地方政府善用資料中心帶來的經濟效益。
「你們必須善用資料中心。讓它們付錢給你們，讓它們為你們的社區付費。」他表示，「但要把握機會，不要把它們拒於門外。」
這番表態延續川普對美中人工智慧競爭的關注。他多次強調，美國必須在這場競賽中勝出，並以「超級智慧」(Super Intelligence，SI) 稱呼人工智慧 (AI)。
川普於週四晚間結束菲律賓與中國行程、返回華府。出訪期間，他與多位國際領袖會面，包括中國國家主席習近平及俄羅斯總統普丁。
川普透露，習近平曾「恭喜」美國在 AI 發展上的表現，也認同使用 SI 這個名稱。
「就像他說的，這比較準確。它是超級的，不是人工智慧。它不是人工的，而是超級的。」川普說，隨後又補上一句：「問題是，它可能太超級了。」
另外，川普提到，兩人同意共同為 AI 設立安全規範，但未在這段談話中進一步說明具體措施。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday (the 20th) that he will not allow American companies to build data centers overseas and threatened to levy "massive taxes" on non‑compliant firms, demanding that investment stay in the United States. Analysts say the proposal will inevitably add a policy variable to the future rollout of data centers by U.S. firms in Taiwan.
However, Trump admitted he has not yet discussed the idea with his staff, and it remains unclear whether any restrictions would cover Taiwan, existing projects or collaborative development models.
At a White House press briefing on Friday, Trump said: "We will not allow our companies to build data centers abroad. We will not let that happen."
He likened data‑center investment to the past offshoring of the chip industry, arguing that allowing chips and other sectors to move overseas caused serious damage to the country.
"They let chips and all kinds of things happen that way, and that is extremely destructive to our nation. That's when we started falling behind," Trump said.

He quickly added, "This is brand‑new, but I haven't even told my staff about it," indicating that the concept of restricting overseas data‑center investment still requires further government clarification on how it would be implemented.
Trump said that any U.S. company that still builds a data center abroad would face a "massive tax burden."
He also warned that if these data centers are allowed to locate in other countries, "China will take them all," though he did not elaborate on what he meant.
Trump's proposal is sure to add a policy variable to the future rollout of data centers by U.S. firms in Taiwan.
For Taiwan, Microsoft’s (MSFT‑US) data‑center expansion is a development to watch.

Microsoft Taiwan general manager Bian Zhixiang said in September that, in response to AI compute demand outpacing supply for the next two to three years, Microsoft is actively expanding its data‑center footprint in Taiwan, growing from two sites to four.
If U.S. measures later cover new overseas facilities or expansion investments, the related construction and capital allocation may need to be reassessed.
Alphabet (GOOGL‑US), Google’s parent, has potential data‑center plans in Tainan and Yunlin, which could also face new policy uncertainty.

In addition, Amazon’s (AMZN‑US) AWS launched the Asia‑Pacific (Taipei) region in June 2025 and pledged to invest over $5 billion long‑term in Taiwan for data‑center construction, networking, operations and maintenance.
Thus, whether future policy only limits new builds or also includes expansion of existing sites will affect how these companies evaluate their Taiwan deployments.

Equally noteworthy is how the policy defines a company’s role. For example, Nvidia (NVDA‑US) is involved in Foxconn’s AI super‑computing center in Taiwan, but the project is led by Foxconn’s ecosystem rather than a direct U.S. investment model.

It remains unclear whether the U.S. will restrict equipment supply, technology cooperation, colocation or compute‑power purchases; Trump gave no details, so it cannot yet be determined which collaborations would be affected.

To keep investment domestic, Trump emphasized on Thursday that many regions in the United States are ready to host data centers, and companies need not turn overseas simply because some locales are unwelcoming.
"We want them to build here. If they don’t go to Texas or California, then they go to West Virginia," he said. "We have a lot of places that really want them, and they’re great places."

Trump cited Loudoun County, Virginia – a hotspot for data centers – saying the area has "made so much money it doesn’t know what to do with it," and urged local governments to make the most of the economic benefits.
"You have to make good use of data centers. Let them pay you, let them pay for your community," he said. "But seize the opportunity and don’t shut them out."
The remarks continue Trump’s focus on the U.S.–China AI competition. He has repeatedly stressed that America must win this race and refers to artificial intelligence as "Super Intelligence" (SI).

Trump concluded his Thursday evening trip, returning to Washington after stops in the Philippines and China, where he met several world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump disclosed that Xi had "congratulated" the United States on its AI progress and also endorsed the use of the term SI.
"Just like he said, it’s more accurate. It’s super, not artificial intelligence. It’s not artificial, it’s super," Trump said, adding, "The problem is, it might be too super."
He also mentioned that the two leaders agreed to jointly establish safety standards for AI, though he gave no further details on specific measures.

items.title: 波蘭指控：俄製Kh-101飛彈又來 可能不只一枚
items.title_en: Poland Accuses: Russian‑made Kh‑101 Missile Returns, Possibly More Than One
paras: 波蘭20日（周五）表示，在俄羅斯連夜對烏克蘭發動襲擊期間，至少有一枚俄羅斯飛彈擊中波蘭東南部，波方正在調查三處撞擊地點。
波蘭國防部長瓦迪斯瓦夫·科西尼亞克-卡梅什說：「目前發現了三處撞擊地點。在諾維利波維茨（Nowy Lipowiec），我們已經能夠確認，擊中該地的是一枚Kh-101飛彈；第二處地點也有飛彈撞擊跡象；第三處地點很可能是一架噴氣式無人機。」
他說道：「沒有人受傷，我們也沒發現任何基礎設施遭破壞。」
這是波蘭方面今年來第二次指控俄方Kh-101飛彈墜落境內，此前一次是在7月30日，當時波方稱東部盧布林省塔納瓦-科洛尼亞附近發現一枚俄製Kh-101飛彈。
《France 24》指出，自烏克蘭戰爭爆發以來，俄方無人機多次誤入北約（NATO）東翼國家的領空，加劇了俄羅斯與北約的緊張關係，也引發外界對戰火可能蔓延的擔憂。
paras_en: Poland said on Friday the 20th that during Russia’s overnight attacks on Ukraine, at least one Russian missile struck southeastern Poland, and Polish authorities are investigating three impact sites.

Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak‑Kamień said, “We have identified three impact locations. In Nowy Lipowiec we have confirmed that the strike was caused by a Kh‑101 missile; the second site also shows evidence of a missile impact; the third site was likely hit by a jet‑powered unmanned aircraft.”
He added, “No one was injured and we did not find any damage to infrastructure.”

This is the second time this year that Poland has accused Russia of a Kh‑101 missile falling on its territory, the first being on July 30 when Polish officials said a Russian‑made Kh‑101 was found near Tanawa‑Kolonia in the eastern Lublin province.

France 24 noted that since the outbreak of the war in Ukraine, Russian drones have repeatedly entered the airspace of NATO’s eastern flank countries, heightening tensions between Russia and NATO and raising concerns that the fighting could spread further.

items.title: AI業務狂飆 輝達估值竟低於2013年！市場重評AI龍頭
items.title_en: AI Business Soars, NVIDIA Valuation Falls Below 2013 Levels! Market Reassesses AI Leader
paras: 輝達 (NVIDIA) (NVDA-US)正處於人工智慧產業高速成長的核心，AI業務持續創造數百億美元營收，然而公司股票估值卻已壓縮至低於2013年底的水準。當時輝達的業務規模僅是如今的一小部分，如今卻出現營運表現與股票估值背離的現象，也讓市場重新思考，華爾街是否對這家AI晶片龍頭過度保守。
輝達11月17日公布2027會計年度第三季財報，營收達1158億美元，年增103%，季增20%。其中，資料中心業務營收達1076億美元，年增110%，仍是公司最主要的成長引擎。
獲利表現同樣強勁，第三季淨利從去年同期的319億美元增至653億美元，超過一倍；稀釋後每股盈餘 (EPS) 達2.70美元，年增108%，顯示AI運算需求仍持續轉化為實際營收與獲利。
展望下一季，輝達預估第四季營收約1300億美元，上下浮動3%，預測區間約為1261億至1339億美元。這一季將比一般季度多一週，且財測假設不包含來自中國的資料中心運算營收，顯示公司在未計入中國相關收入的情況下，仍預期業務維持強勁成長。
輝達臨時執行長兼財務長Colette Kress在財報聲明中表示，公司成長動能真實且持續，Vera Rubin產品路線圖仍按計畫推進。公司並確認，下一代Vera Rubin NVL72平台已開始出貨，為後續AI運算產品世代建立基礎。
然而，營運高速成長並未阻止股票估值持續下滑。根據Benzinga Pro數據，輝達目前追蹤本益比為15.68倍，預估本益比僅9.24倍，PEG比率則為0.178倍。PEG比率用來比較本益比與預期獲利成長，數值偏低代表股價相對預期成長的估值較低。
歷史數據更凸顯這次估值修正的幅度。根據CompaniesMarketCap資料，輝達2013年底本益比為19.6倍，2014年底為18.3倍，2018年底則為17.1倍。以Benzinga Pro目前的15.68倍計算，已低於上述三個歷史基準。
從近五年變化來看，輝達本益比曾在2023年一度突破200倍，隨後於2024年至2026年一路下滑。這反映投資人對AI產業的成長預期，已從過去願意支付極高溢價，轉向更重視獲利能否持續、資本支出是否合理，以及未來需求能否支撐目前的營運規模。
股價近期也承受沉重賣壓。根據Benzinga Pro報價，輝達周五 (20日) 盤中一度下跌6.95%，報135.83美元，顯示即使財報營收、獲利及下一季展望均維持強勁，市場仍未完全消除對AI投資熱潮可持續性的疑慮。
不過，低本益比並不必然代表股票遭到低估。估值下降也可能反映投資人開始擔心AI基礎設施支出放緩、競爭加劇，或大型客戶對資本支出的態度轉趨謹慎。若未來需求成長不如預期，市場目前採用的獲利預估也可能下修，進而改變本益比所呈現的便宜程度。
因此，投資人接下來需要關注幾項指標，包括資料中心業務成長速度、毛利率變化、大型客戶的資本支出，以及管理層對未來營收的財測。這些因素將決定輝達目前的低估值，究竟反映市場過度悲觀，還是投資人正在重新評估AI基礎建設熱潮的持續時間。
對輝達而言，當前最值得關注的矛盾在於，AI業務仍以三位數年增率擴張，股票估值卻已回落至十多年前的水準。若公司能持續將AI需求轉化為營收與獲利，估值落差可能成為市場重新評價的契機；但若AI投資熱潮降溫，低本益比也未必能阻止股價進一步修正。
paras_en: NVIDIA (NVDA-US) is at the core of the fast‑growing artificial‑intelligence industry, with its AI business generating hundreds of billions of dollars in revenue, yet the stock’s valuation has compressed to below the level seen at the end of 2013. Back then NVIDIA’s scale was only a fraction of today’s, and now a disconnect between operating performance and stock valuation is prompting the market to rethink whether Wall Street has been overly conservative on the AI chip leader.

On November 17, NVIDIA reported its fiscal 2027 third‑quarter results, posting revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year‑over‑year and 20% sequentially. Data‑center revenue reached $107.6 billion, a 110% annual increase, remaining the company’s primary growth engine.

Profitability was equally strong, with third‑quarter net income rising from $31.9 billion a year earlier to $65.3 billion, more than double. Diluted earnings per share were $2.70, up 108% year‑over‑year, showing AI compute demand continues to translate into real revenue and profit.

Looking ahead to the next quarter, NVIDIA forecasts fourth‑quarter revenue of roughly $130 billion, give or take 3%, i.e., a range of $126.1 billion to $133.9 billion. This quarter will be a week longer than a typical quarter, and the outlook excludes data‑center revenue from China, indicating the company still expects strong growth even without Chinese‑related income.

Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said in the earnings release that the company’s growth momentum is genuine and ongoing, and the Vera Rubin product roadmap remains on schedule. She confirmed that the next‑generation Vera Rubin NVL72 platform has already begun shipping, laying the foundation for future AI compute generations.

However, rapid operating growth has not stopped the stock’s valuation from sliding. According to Benzinga Pro, NVIDIA’s current trailing P/E is 15.68×, forward P/E is only 9.24×, and its PEG ratio stands at 0.178×. A low PEG indicates the share price is cheap relative to expected earnings growth.

Historical data highlight the magnitude of this valuation adjustment. CompaniesMarketCap shows NVIDIA’s year‑end 2013 P/E was 19.6×, 2014’s was 18.3×, and 2018’s was 17.1×. At today’s 15.68×, the valuation is already below those three historic benchmarks.

Over the past five years, NVIDIA’s P/E peaked above 200× in 2023 before falling steadily from 2024 through 2026. This reflects investors shifting from paying extreme premiums for AI growth to focusing more on sustainable profitability, reasonable capex, and whether future demand can support the current scale.

The stock has also faced heavy selling pressure recently. Benzinga Pro data show that on Friday the 20th, NVIDIA fell as much as 6.95% intraday to $135.83, indicating that even with strong revenue, profit and next‑quarter outlook, the market has not fully dispelled doubts about the durability of the AI investment boom.

Nevertheless, a low P/E does not automatically mean the stock is undervalued. The valuation decline may also signal investor concerns about slowing AI infrastructure spending, heightened competition, or large customers becoming more cautious with capex. If demand growth falls short of expectations, profit forecasts could be revised down, altering the perceived cheapness of the P/E.

Consequently, investors will need to watch several indicators, including data‑center growth rates, margin trends, large‑customer capex behavior, and management’s revenue guidance. These factors will determine whether NVIDIA’s low valuation reflects excessive market pessimism or a genuine reassessment of the AI infrastructure boom’s longevity.

For NVIDIA, the key paradox is that AI revenue continues to expand at triple‑digit annual rates while the stock’s valuation has slipped back to levels seen more than a decade ago. If the company can keep turning AI demand into revenue and profit, the valuation gap could become a catalyst for a market re‑rating; but if the AI hype cools, a low P/E may not prevent further price corrections.

items.title: 加密私訊仍怕AI看螢幕！Signal推預設封鎖截圖 批Siri與Gemini「尤其令人擔心」
items.title_en: Encrypted Messaging Still Fears AI Watching Screens! Signal to Enable Screenshot Blocking by Default, Criticizes Siri and Gemini as “Especially Worrying”
paras: 加密通訊軟體Signal 20日宣布，將預設開啟截圖封鎖功能，防止AI代理讀取手機上的私人訊息，並警告科技業把AI嵌入消費裝置的趨勢，正在侵蝕隱私保障。
Signal總裁Meredith Whittaker坦言新防護仍「不完整」，呼籲蘋果(AAPL-US)、Alphabet(GOOGL-US)與微軟(MSFT-US)提供更具體的阻擋工具。
Signal同時要求三家公司揭露其AI代理的運作與資料存取方式，讓開發者能評估代理接觸了哪些資料，並據此調整系統。
Signal點名作業系統內建的蘋果Siri AI與Google Gemini Intelligence特別令人憂心，稱這類代理式AI整合「對隱私日益敵意」，對Signal構成「生存威脅」。
新功能預設阻擋手機截圖存取。當Signal偵測到截圖嘗試或AI助理試圖存取螢幕，用戶會收到彈出視窗，可選擇是否關閉封鎖，實際形式因裝置而異。
《路透社》本週稍早披露，Meta(META-US)的Muse代理繞過官方Connector工具，利用初始設定取得的系統層級權限，讀取蘋果電腦與Android手機上的Signal訊息。
在macOS上，Muse挪用蘋果為身障用戶設計的輔助使用與截圖工具，對Signal聊天截圖、擷取文字後複製到Muse應用內。蘋果本週更新雖堵住此路徑，但新增的代理權限組仍提供類似能力。
Meta回應《路透社》報導時表示，AI代理需要看到並操作電腦才能代用戶工作，Muse只能透過用戶明確授權的權限存取其他App。蘋果、Google與微軟未立即回應置評請求。
Signal去年已在Windows平台封鎖微軟Recall AI截圖，但表示在macOS上無法可靠提供同類防護；Signal由非營利基金會持有，以端到端加密保護訊息。
Signal主張，開發者應有簡單直接的方式，讓App完全退出AI助理對螢幕讀取、通知與檔案系統的資料處理。
paras_en: Signal announced on the 20th that it will enable a screenshot‑blocking feature by default to prevent AI agents from reading private messages on phones, warning that the tech industry’s trend of embedding AI into consumer devices is eroding privacy protections.
Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker admitted the new protection is still “incomplete” and called on Apple (AAPL‑US), Alphabet (GOOGL‑US) and Microsoft (MSFT‑US) to provide more concrete blocking tools.

Signal also demanded that the three companies disclose how their AI agents operate and access data so developers can assess what information the agents have touched and adjust their systems accordingly.

Signal singled out the built‑in Apple Siri AI and Google Gemini Intelligence as particularly concerning, saying such agent‑style AI integrations are becoming “increasingly hostile to privacy” and pose a “survival threat” to Signal.

The new feature defaults to blocking apps from accessing screenshots. When Signal detects a screenshot attempt or an AI assistant trying to read the screen, users see a pop‑up window and can choose whether to lift the block; the exact implementation varies by device.

Reuters earlier this week reported that Meta’s (META‑US) Muse agent bypassed the official Connector tool, using system‑level permissions obtained at setup to read Signal messages on both Apple computers and Android phones.

On macOS, Muse hijacked Apple’s accessibility and screenshot tools designed for users with disabilities, capturing Signal chat screenshots, extracting text, and copying it into the Muse app; Apple’s update this week closed that pathway, but a newly added agent‑permission group still grants similar capabilities.

Meta responded to the Reuters report by saying AI agents need to see and manipulate the computer to act on a user’s behalf, and that Muse can only access other apps through permissions explicitly granted by the user; Apple, Google and Microsoft did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Signal said it blocked Microsoft’s Recall AI screenshot feature on Windows last year, but that it cannot reliably provide the same protection on macOS; Signal is owned by a nonprofit foundation and protects messages with end‑to‑end encryption.
Signal argues that developers should have a simple, direct way to let apps fully opt out of AI assistants reading screens, notifications and file‑system data.

paras_en: US‑China competition for AI dominance shares a common bottom line: President Trump and President Xi have agreed that major military actions cannot be decided autonomously by AI.

items.title: 黃仁勳離任後 輝達面臨更棘手危機：核心工程師恐遭競爭對手挖角
items.title_en: After Jensen Huang Steps Down, Nvidia Faces a More Tricky Crisis: Core Engineers May Be Poached by Rivals
paras: 輝達 (NVIDIA) (NVDA-US)在創辦人黃仁勳遭董事會解除執行長職務後，面臨的危機恐怕不只股價重挫，更深層的隱憂是核心工程師是否會跟著離開。對一家高度仰賴技術創新、並以晶片與軟體整合建立競爭優勢的企業而言，人才流失可能直接牽動未來數年的產品研發與AI布局。
自董事會上週宣布解除黃仁勳職務以來，輝達市值已蒸發約5,000億美元，引發員工、投資人及科技業人士強烈反彈。數千名員工聯署要求黃仁勳復職，部分員工公開批評董事會決定，也已有員工宣布離職。
黃仁勳週二表示，若董事會批准，他將很榮幸重返執行長職位，並提到自己收到員工、投資人、商業夥伴及客戶的大量支持聲音。不過，在公司領導權出現變動後，輝達能否留住打造其技術優勢的核心團隊，已成為投資人更需要關注的問題。
Melius Research首席科技分析師Ben Reitzes在輝達本週財報電話會議前指出，臨時管理團隊最優先的任務之一，就是防止工程師離職。他認為，對長期投資人而言，公司的產品路線圖才是最重要的關鍵，市場需要了解管理層將如何留住人才，確保既有研發計畫不受影響。
這項風險之所以重要，在於輝達的競爭優勢並非只來自單一晶片，而是晶片、軟體及其他技術系統高度整合的產品架構。公司從遊戲顯示卡製造商轉型為AI運算基礎設施核心供應商，仰賴長期技術投資，以及管理層對運算趨勢與市場需求的前瞻判斷。
Circular Technology研究主管Brad Gastwirth指出，若輝達流失5至10名關鍵技術領導者，尤其是負責架構決策或重大產品轉型的人才，就可能造成遠超離職人數本身的衝擊。Synovus投資專業人士Christopher Brown也認為，輝達產品體系高度集中，代表技術人才流失可能使公司的風險同步集中。
對科技企業而言，技術領導者不只是負責現有產品開發，更必須提前數年判斷技術方向，在市場需求尚未完全明朗時，就決定下一代產品的架構與研發路線。黃仁勳過去正是這套體系的重要推動者，他不僅帶領公司轉型，也持續在AI技術商業價值尚未完全確立前投入資源。
黃仁勳離任後，競爭對手可能趁輝達內部動盪展開挖角。Gastwirth預期，超微 (AMD) (AMD-US)、博通 (Broadcom) (AVGO-US)、大型雲端服務商及AI新創企業，都可能積極招募輝達工程師。Brown也認為，競爭對手鎖定輝達技術人才的招募行動幾乎難以避免。
特斯拉 (Tesla) (TSLA-US)執行長馬斯克也曾談及黃仁勳與員工之間的關係。他指出，許多輝達員工是因為黃仁勳而加入公司，並出於對他的忠誠，拒絕其他企業提供的更高薪酬。這也凸顯黃仁勳的影響力不只在企業決策，更深入員工文化與人才凝聚力。
員工的反應同樣反映這種連結。已離職的輝達機器人研究員Darrell Dai在離職聲明中，肯定黃仁勳營造鼓勵工程師探索、承擔風險並從錯誤中學習的工作環境，也讚揚他願意在技術商業價值尚未明朗時就投入資源。輝達研究科學家Shang-Wen Li則在社群平台X公開表示，對董事會的決定深感失望。
面對內部不安，臨時執行長兼財務長Colette Kress已開始透過薪酬措施穩定團隊。她在週三舉行的全員大會宣布，將原定較晚時間發放的加薪及額外股票獎勵提前至12月，並強調公司的技術路線圖及客戶關係都不會改變。
然而，薪酬能否真正留住核心人才，仍存在疑問。一名參與全員大會的員工表示，更好的待遇短期內確實具有吸引力，但未必足以成為長期留任的理由。過去十年輝達股價大幅上漲，已讓不少資深員工累積可觀財富，部分人甚至擁有相當程度的財務自由，額外股票獎勵的吸引力可能因此下降。
對這些工程師而言，未來技術方向、研發自主權，以及公司是否仍有能力推動創新，可能比短期薪酬更重要。若員工認為原有技術願景與領導文化已經改變，即使公司提高薪資，也未必能完全消除離職意願。
Kress在華爾街具有良好聲譽，但她過去的職涯主要集中在財務管理領域，外界因此關注她能否承擔制定輝達未來十年技術及產品路線圖的重任。董事會目前也正尋找正式執行長，內部及外部人選都在考慮範圍內。
Gastwirth認為，黃仁勳的價值不只是管理公司，而是具備預判運算及AI技術發展方向的能力，並能讓輝達提前數年完成布局。當下一代AI技術逐漸成形，若公司同時失去黃仁勳及其他關鍵技術領導者，未來的產品架構、研發節奏與技術判斷能力都可能受到影響。
因此，輝達眼前真正需要處理的，並不只是尋找下一任執行長，而是如何延續黃仁勳建立的技術文化與創新體系。若核心工程師陸續流向競爭對手，公司失去的將不只是人力，更可能是維持AI技術領先地位所需的專業知識與長期戰略能力。
paras_en: Nvidia (NVDA-US) faces a crisis that may go beyond a sharp stock price drop after its founder Jensen Huang was removed as CEO by the board; the deeper concern is whether core engineers will follow him out. For a company that relies heavily on technological innovation and builds competitive advantage through chip‑software integration, talent loss could directly affect product development and AI strategy for years to come.

Since the board announced Huang’s removal last week, Nvidia’s market value has evaporated about $500 billion, sparking strong backlash from employees, investors and tech industry observers. Thousands of staff signed a petition demanding Huang’s reinstatement, some publicly criticized the board’s decision, and a number of employees have already resigned.

Huang said on Tuesday that, if the board approves, he would be honored to return as CEO and noted the overwhelming support he has received from employees, investors, business partners and customers. However, with the leadership change, investors are now more focused on whether Nvidia can retain the core team that built its technological edge.

Melius Research chief technology analyst Ben Reitzes told the earnings call this week that one of the interim management team’s top priorities is preventing engineer turnover. He believes that for long‑term investors the company’s product roadmap is the key issue, and the market needs to understand how the new leadership will keep talent and protect existing R&D plans.

The risk matters because Nvidia’s competitive edge does not stem from a single chip but from a highly integrated architecture of chips, software and other technologies. The firm has shifted from a gaming graphics card maker to a core supplier of AI compute infrastructure, relying on long‑term tech investment and forward‑looking judgments about compute trends and market demand.

Circular Technology research lead Brad Gastwirth warned that losing just five to ten key technical leaders—especially those responsible for architecture decisions or major product transitions—could have impacts far greater than the headcount loss itself. Synovus investment professional Christopher Brown added that Nvidia’s product ecosystem is highly concentrated, meaning talent loss could concentrate risk as well.

For tech companies, technical leaders are not only responsible for current product development but must also forecast technology directions years in advance, deciding on next‑generation architectures and R&D paths before market demand is fully clear. Huang has been a driving force of this system, leading the transformation and investing in AI technology even before its commercial value was fully proven.

After Huang’s departure, rivals may seize the internal turmoil to poach Nvidia staff. Gastwirth expects AMD (AMD-US), Broadcom (AVGO-US), large cloud service providers and AI startups to actively recruit Nvidia engineers. Brown agrees that competitors’ attempts to hire Nvidia’s technical talent are almost inevitable.

Tesla (TSLA-US) CEO Elon Musk also commented on the relationship between Huang and Nvidia employees. He said many staff joined because of Huang and, out of loyalty to him, turned down higher salaries offered by other firms. This underscores Huang’s influence beyond corporate decisions, extending into employee culture and talent cohesion.

The employee response mirrors this bond. Former Nvidia robotics researcher Darrell Dai, in his resignation statement, praised the environment Huang fostered—encouraging engineers to explore, take risks and learn from mistakes—and lauded his willingness to fund projects before their commercial value was clear. Nvidia research scientist Shang‑Wen Li posted on X expressing deep disappointment with the board’s decision.

Facing internal unease, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress has begun using compensation measures to steady the team. At a company‑wide meeting on Wednesday she announced that salary increases and additional stock awards originally slated for a later date will be moved up to December, and she stressed that the technical roadmap and customer relationships will remain unchanged.

Nevertheless, doubts remain about whether compensation alone can retain core talent. An employee who attended the all‑hands said better pay is attractive in the short term but may not be enough for long‑term retention. Over the past decade Nvidia’s soaring stock price has given many senior staff substantial wealth and even financial independence, reducing the lure of extra stock grants.

For these engineers, future technology direction, R&D autonomy and the company’s ability to keep innovating may matter more than short‑term pay. If staff feel the original technical vision and leadership culture have shifted, higher salaries may not fully erase their desire to leave.

Kress enjoys a strong reputation on Wall Street, but her career has been focused on financial management, prompting questions about her capacity to shape Nvidia’s ten‑year technical and product roadmap. The board is also searching for a permanent CEO, considering both internal and external candidates.

Gastwirth argues that Huang’s value lies not just in running the company but in anticipating compute and AI trends and enabling Nvidia to lay out its roadmap years ahead. As the next generation of AI technology takes shape, losing both Huang and other key technical leaders could affect product architecture, development pace and technical judgment.

Thus, Nvidia’s immediate challenge is not merely finding a new CEO but preserving the technology culture and innovation system Huang built. If core engineers gradually move to rivals, the loss will be more than manpower—it could erode the specialized knowledge and long‑term strategic capability needed to maintain AI leadership.

items.title: 美參院通過能源許可改革 鬆綁基建審查、資料中心須自付能源成本
items.title_en: U.S. Senate Passes Energy Permit Reform, Loosening Infrastructure Review and Requiring Data Centers to Pay Energy Costs
paras: 美國參議院19日以62票對33票通過兩黨能源許可改革法案，加速電廠、輸電線等能源基礎建設的審查，並要求資料中心為所用能源付費，法案接下來送交眾議院。
這是期中選舉後國會通過的首項重大法案。AI熱潮推升用電需求與電價，選民對資料中心的不滿，成為民主黨在期中選舉勝出的助力之一。
這項《2026年兩黨美國可負擔與就業法案》將修改國家環境政策法、淨水法與瀕危物種法相關規定，縮短大型能源項目審查時程；目前環評程序動輒五年以上。
川普在社群媒體呼籲國會通過，稱法案是「美國能源獨立與主導地位的一大勝利」，可更快興建管線、礦場與電廠，降低美國家庭的能源成本。
表決中15名民主黨議員投下贊成票，包括參院少數黨領袖舒默；共和黨則有密蘇里州Hawley與南達科他州Rounds兩人反對。
環保團體批評修法將鎖定化石燃料開發、削弱環境保障並限制環評司法審查。環境誠信計畫執行長Jen Duggan稱，這是「送給美國最大污染者的禮物」。
民主黨參議員Merkley與Wyden推動多項修正案，包括禁止在公共土地興建資料中心，最終未獲表決。Merkley批評法案一面推動再生能源、一面助長化石燃料。
法案下一關是眾議院。眾院去年通過的是範圍較限縮、對產業較友善的版本，兩院版本仍須協調。
支持法案的民主黨氣候鷹派Whitehouse表示，此案是氣候與環境立法的「地板，不是天花板」，寄望民主黨未來兩年以更大優勢推動更多立法。
paras_en: On the 19th, the U.S. Senate approved a bipartisan energy permitting reform bill by a vote of 62‑33, speeding up reviews of energy infrastructure such as power plants and transmission lines and requiring data centers to pay for the energy they consume. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives.

It is the first major piece of legislation passed by Congress since the midterm elections. A surge in AI usage has driven up electricity demand and prices, and voter frustration with data centers helped the Democrats win the midterms.

The "2026 Bipartisan American Affordability and Employment Act" will amend the National Environmental Policy Act, the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act to shorten review timelines for large energy projects, which currently can take more than five years under existing environmental‑review procedures.

Former President Trump urged Congress on social media to pass the bill, calling it “a huge win for American energy independence and leadership,” saying it will accelerate pipelines, mines and power plants and lower household energy costs.

Fifteen Democratic senators voted in favor, including Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer, while Republicans Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri and Senator John Rounds of South Dakota opposed the measure.

Environmental groups criticized the amendment, saying it locks in fossil‑fuel development, weakens environmental protections and limits judicial review of environmental assessments. Jen Duggan, CEO of the Environmental Integrity Project, called it “a gift to America’s biggest polluters.”

Democratic senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden pushed several amendments, such as banning data‑center construction on public lands, but none were adopted. Merkley warned that the bill promotes renewable energy on one hand while bolstering fossil fuels on the other.
The bill’s next hurdle is the House of Representatives. The House passed a narrower, more industry‑friendly version last year, so the two chambers will need to reconcile their versions.

Democratic climate hawk John Whitehouse, who supports the bill, said it represents a “floor, not a ceiling” for climate and environmental legislation, hoping the Democrats can leverage a stronger majority over the next two years to pass more ambitious laws.

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元走軟 日元、瑞郎強升 比特幣跌破6萬美元
items.title_en: <New York Forex> Dollar Weakens, Yen and Franc Rally, Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000
paras: 美元指數週五 (20 日) 小幅走低，終止連八個交易日上漲。市場對人工智慧 (AI) 產業的疑慮持續衝擊全球股市，資金轉進美國公債避險，帶動殖利率下滑，推升日元與瑞郎。不過，聯準會 (Fed) 官員持續釋出鷹派訊號，加上市場降低對風險貨幣的持有意願，限制美元跌幅。
美股尾盤時段，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣表現的美元指數下跌 0.07%，至 103.87，仍接近前一交易日觸及、2025 年 4 月以來的最高水準。
美元這波漲勢在 11 月 10 日加速，當時美國通膨數據高於預期，強化市場對聯準會進一步緊縮政策的押注。聯準會理事沃勒 (Christopher Waller) 也表示，應考慮在 12 月升息 2 碼。
Bannockburn Capital Markets 首席市場策略師 Marc Chandler 表示：「我認為美元的上漲動能已經停滯……但現在就認定美元已經見頂，還有點太早。」
美債避險買盤湧現 日元、瑞郎受惠
AI 相關疑慮持續壓抑全球股市，Anthropic (ANT-US) 週四創紀錄的上市案，也未能有效提振投資人信心。資金週五轉向公債避險，推動美債殖利率下滑，提高日元與瑞郎等低利率貨幣的相對吸引力。
Chandler 表示：「當美國利率下降時，低收益貨幣就顯得更具吸引力。」
美元兌瑞郎下跌 0.51%，報 1 美元可兌換 0.8396 瑞郎；美元兌日元下跌 0.73%，報 1 美元可兌換 158.50 日元，顯示瑞郎與日元雙雙兌美元升值。日元匯價仍接近日本當局今年 7 月進場干預、支撐日元時的水準。
除了美債殖利率下降，日本通膨數據也提供日元支撐。日本 10 月核心消費者物價指數 (CPI) 年增率加速至 2.2%，連續第二個月高於日本銀行的 2% 目標，顯示物價壓力擴散，強化日銀近期升息的理由。
Chandler 指出：「日元今天走強，受到美國利率下降，以及日本 10 月 CPI 表現強勁的帶動。」
凱投宏觀分析師認為，日元近期的疲弱走勢不太可能持續。
隨著日本長期通膨預期已接近目標，殖利率進一步上升將主要反映實質利率提高，加上該機構預期美債殖利率將下降，兩項因素應有利日元。
聯準會維持鷹派 川普再批利率過高
儘管美元回落，策略師認為，聯準會偏向升息的政策前景仍將提供支撐。
ING 全球市場主管 Chris Turner 表示，雖然目前支持股市再度大幅修正的理由有限，但「聯準會沒有理由在短期內放棄鷹派論調」。
他指出，下週公布的美國個人消費支出物價指數 (PCE)，可能進一步確認聯準會有必要採取行動。
聯準會理事庫克 (Lisa Cook) 週五也支持進一步升息，表示目前政策利率不足以因應通膨，並稱她對通膨水準「深感憂慮」。
美國總統川普則在週五記者會上表示，目前利率過高，並批評聯準會具有「政治性」。
其他主要貨幣方面，歐元兌美元小跌至 1.0963 美元；英鎊兌美元下跌至 1.3080 美元，仍徘徊在一年低點附近。澳元與紐元分別下跌 0.71% 及 0.36%，反映風險貨幣持續承壓。
加密貨幣也遭拋售浪潮襲擊。
隨著投資人擔憂 AI 相關資產估值過高，賣壓擴及其他風險資產，比特幣週五跌破 6 萬美元，為 7 月以來首見，報導更新時下跌約 6%，至 57,939 美元。
依台北時間週六上午 5 時許最新報價，主要匯率表現如下：

紐元兌美元下跌 0.36%，至 1 紐元兌 0.5464 美元。
美元兌日元下跌 0.73%，至 1 美元兌 158.50 日元。
美元兌瑞郎下跌 0.51%，至 1 美元兌 0.8396 瑞郎。
美元兌加元上漲 0.03%，至 1 美元兌 1.4344 加元。
paras_en: The U.S. dollar index slipped slightly on Friday (the 20th), ending an eight‑day winning streak. Ongoing concerns about the artificial‑intelligence (AI) sector continued to weigh on global equities, prompting a shift into U.S. Treasury safe‑haven assets, which pushed yields lower and boosted the yen and Swiss franc. However, hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and reduced appetite for risk currencies limited the dollar's decline.

In the late‑session of U.S. equities, the dollar index, which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, fell 0.07% to 103.87, still near the highest level reached on the previous trading day, the peak since April 2025.

The dollar's recent rally accelerated on November 10 when U.S. inflation data came in hotter than expected, strengthening market bets on further Fed tightening. Fed Governor Christopher Waller also said a 25‑basis‑point rate hike in December should be considered.
Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets, said: “I think the dollar’s upward momentum has stalled… but it’s still a bit early to declare that the dollar has peaked.”
U.S. Treasury safe‑haven buying lifts yen and franc

AI‑related worries kept global equities under pressure, and even Anthropic’s (ANT‑US) record‑setting IPO on Thursday failed to lift investor confidence. On Friday, funds moved into Treasury safe‑haven assets, driving U.S. bond yields lower and raising the relative appeal of low‑yield currencies such as the yen and Swiss franc.
Chandler added: “When U.S. rates fall, low‑yield currencies become more attractive.”

The dollar fell 0.51% against the franc to $1 = 0.8396 CHF, and 0.73% against the yen to $1 = 158.50 JPY, indicating that both currencies appreciated versus the greenback. The yen rate remains close to the level at which Japanese authorities intervened in July to support the currency.

In addition to falling U.S. yields, Japanese inflation data also supported the yen. Japan’s October core consumer‑price index (CPI) annualised rate accelerated to 2.2%, the second consecutive month above the Bank of Japan’s 2% target, showing broader price pressure and bolstering the case for a recent BOJ rate hike.
Chandler noted: “The yen’s strength today is driven by falling U.S. rates and the strong October CPI reading in Japan.”
Macro analyst at KGI believes the yen’s recent weakness is unlikely to persist.

With Japan’s long‑term inflation expectations now near target, any further rise in yields will mainly reflect higher real rates, and the institution expects U.S. Treasury yields to fall – two factors that should benefit the yen.
Fed Maintains Hawkish Stance as Trump Again Criticises High Rates
Even though the dollar retreated, strategists say the Fed’s bias toward rate hikes will continue to provide support.

Chris Turner, head of global markets at ING, said that while there are limited reasons at present to justify another sharp equity correction, “the Fed has no reason to abandon its hawkish tone in the short term.”
He added that next week’s U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index could further confirm the Fed’s need to act.
Fed Governor Lisa Cook also backed further tightening on Friday, saying current policy rates are insufficient to curb inflation and expressing “deep concern” about inflation levels.
Former President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that rates are currently too high and criticized the Fed as being “political.”

Among other major currencies, the euro slipped to $1.0963, the pound fell to $1.3080, hovering near a one‑year low, while the Australian and New Zealand dollars dropped 0.71% and 0.36% respectively, reflecting continued pressure on risk assets.
Cryptocurrencies also came under selling pressure.

As investors worried that AI‑related assets were overvalued, selling spread to other risk assets and Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday – the first time since July – dropping about 6% to $57,939 at the time of the update.

The euro slipped 0.04% to $1.0963 per euro.
The pound fell 0.06% to $1.3080 per pound.
The Australian dollar dropped 0.71% to $0.6612 per Aussie.
The New Zealand dollar fell 0.36% to $0.5464 per kiwi.
The dollar weakened 0.73% to ¥158.50 per dollar.
The dollar weakened 0.51% to CHF 0.8396 per dollar.
The dollar rose 0.03% to C$1.4344 per dollar.

items.title_en: New Taiwan Dollar: Central Bank Strongly Stabilizes, Closes at 32.936, Up 0.6 Points
paras: 台股加權指數今(20)日再度破底，市場出現強烈的去槓桿壓力，單日跌點達2393點，創史上第三大跌點，一周來已跌掉7641點，周跌幅17.5%，台北匯市見到中央銀行全力穩盤調節，新台幣終場收在32.936元，升值0.6分，與股市脫鉤，台北外匯經紀公司成交值則縮至21.02億美元。

paras: 美元週四(19日)兌多數主要貨幣回落，近期漲勢暫歇。人工智慧(AI)公司Anthropic即將掛牌，提振市場風險偏好，削弱美元買盤。不過，聯準會(Fed)官員的鷹派談話與最新會議紀錄，仍使進一步升息的預期支撐美元，美元指數維持在約19個月高點附近。
美股尾盤時段，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.2%，報103.65；歐元兌美元上漲0.2%，報1.1002美元。
美元指數本週觸及2025年4月2日以來最高水準。當時，美國總統川普宣布大規模關稅措施，引發美國資產賣壓。
美元這波漲勢始於11月10日，當時美國通膨數據高於預期，促使投資人提高對聯準會緊縮政策的押注。聯準會理事華勒(Christopher Waller)呼籲採取更積極措施對抗通膨，而10月27日至28日的會議紀錄也顯示，決策官員愈來愈擔心，可能需要進一步緊縮政策。
加拿大豐業銀行首席外匯策略師奧斯本(Shaun Osborne)表示：「美元這段時間已經漲了不少，我認為目前匯價已反映許多利多。」
他指出，美元多頭若要在短期內推升匯價，需要更強的信心或更多利多消息。他並將美元部分回落，歸因於Anthropic首次公開發行(IPO)前，市場風險情緒改善。
Anthropic的IPO定價高於原先行銷區間，帶動週四那斯達克期貨上漲，也提高市場對其上市表現的期待，重新提振AI類股投資情緒。
巴克萊分析師則認為，財政刺激與強勁的AI相關資本支出，反映美國經濟具有韌性，也意味經濟產出高於潛在水準的幅度可能擴大，利率將在更長時間內維持高檔，這些因素均有利美元。
儘管近期科技股遭到拋售，美元仍獲得資金流入支撐。德意志銀行追蹤逾100檔在美國境外註冊的指數股票型基金(ETF)發現，外國投資人過去兩週大舉逢低買進美股，買進力道為今年最強，顯示流向美股的資金也是支撐美元的重要因素。
隨著風險偏好回升、避險需求降溫，日元兌美元走貶。美元兌日元上漲0.4%，報159.905日元兌1美元，中止連續四個交易日下跌。
分析師指出，若AI相關資產再度遭到拋售，避險買盤與資金匯回日本可能支撐日元，但日元兌其他貨幣的升勢，可能比兌美元更為明顯。
澳幣兌美元則大致持平。澳洲10月就業人數連續第二個月減少，失業率升至五年高點，強化市場對當地利率可能已觸頂的看法。
三菱日聯金融集團(MUFG)資深外匯分析師 Lee Hardman表示，市場大幅上調對聯準會升息的預期，正對大宗商品價格及相關貨幣形成壓力。
瑞銀考量澳洲通膨仍高，以及勞動與房市情況惡化，將澳洲央行首次降息時間預測，由明年11月提前至8月，並將預估降息次數由兩次增加至三次。
英鎊兌美元升值0.1%，報1英鎊兌1.3162美元，但英鎊兌歐元則從20個月高點回落。投資人仍看好英國利率前景，同時對歐洲2027年多場重要選舉可能為歐元帶來的阻力保持警戒。
加密貨幣方面，受風險偏好改善帶動，比特幣上漲2.5%，報63,870美元，脫離上週日觸及的四個月低點62,026美元。

paras_en: The dollar fell against most major currencies on Thursday (the 19th), pausing its recent rally. The upcoming IPO of AI company Anthropic lifted market risk appetite and weakened dollar buying pressure. However, hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and the latest meeting minutes still support expectations of further rate hikes, keeping the dollar index near a 19‑month high.
In the late‑day US equity session, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, slipped 0.2% to 103.65, while the euro rose 0.2% to $1.1002.
The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when President Trump announced large‑scale tariff measures that triggered selling pressure on US assets.

The current dollar rally began on November 10, when US inflation data came in above expectations, prompting investors to increase bets on tighter Fed policy. Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for more aggressive action against inflation, and the minutes from the Oct. 27‑28 meeting showed policymakers growing increasingly concerned that further tightening may be needed.

Shaun Osborne, chief FX strategist at Canada’s BMO Capital Markets, said: “The dollar has already risen a lot in recent weeks, and I think the current exchange rates already reflect much of the upside.”

He added that for dollar bulls to push rates higher in the short term they would need stronger conviction or more positive news, and he attributed the dollar’s partial pullback to improved market risk sentiment ahead of Anthropic’s IPO.
Anthropic’s IPO was priced above its initial marketing range, lifting Nasdaq futures on Thursday and raising expectations for its market debut, which revived sentiment toward AI‑related stocks.

Barclays analysts argue that fiscal stimulus and robust AI‑related capital spending show the US economy is resilient, suggesting output may be running above potential for longer, keeping rates high – a backdrop that benefits the dollar.

Despite recent tech‑stock sell‑offs, the dollar continued to attract inflows. Deutsche Bank, tracking over 100 offshore‑registered ETFs, found foreign investors bought US equities in large volumes over the past two weeks – the strongest buying this year – indicating that capital flowing into US stocks also underpins the dollar.
With risk appetite recovering and hedging demand easing, the yen weakened against the dollar. The USD/JPY rose 0.4% to 159.905 yen per dollar, ending a four‑day decline.

Analysts note that if AI‑related assets face another sell‑off, safe‑haven buying and capital returning to Japan could support the yen, but the yen’s gains against other currencies may be more pronounced than against the dollar.

The Australian dollar was roughly flat versus the US dollar. October employment in Australia fell for the second consecutive month, pushing the unemployment rate to a five‑year high and reinforcing market views that local rates may have peaked.
Lee Hardman, senior FX analyst at MUFG, said the market’s sharp upgrade of expectations for Fed rate hikes is putting pressure on commodity prices and related currencies.

UBS, considering still‑elevated Australian inflation and worsening labour and housing conditions, moved its forecast for the Reserve Bank of Australia’s first rate cut from November next year to August and increased the expected number of cuts from two to three.

The pound rose 0.1% to $1.3162, but the GBP/EUR slipped from a 20‑month peak. Investors remain bullish on UK rate prospects while staying cautious about the potential drag on the euro from several major European elections slated for 2027.
In crypto, improved risk appetite lifted Bitcoin 2.5% to $63,870, pulling it out of the four‑month low of $62,026 hit last Sunday.

paras: 美元週三(18日)週三走強，升至19個月來新高，受到美國聯準會(Fed)官員華勒(Christopher Waller)的鷹派談話，以及近期經濟數據影響，市場對下個月升息的預期更加確立。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.2%，報103.78，創2025年4月以來最高。
聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)拒絕提供未來政策指引，使投資人更加依賴經濟數據，以及其他決策官員的談話，來判斷聯準會下一步動向。
華勒接受CNBC訪問時表示，如果央行希望降低通膨，就必須採取更「積極的行動」，包括在12月會議升息半個百分點，或是在會後聲明中引導市場預期，為進一步升息做好準備。
上週公布的通膨數據高於預期，使市場完全反映聯準會12月升息25個基點的預期，同時認為升息50個基點仍存在小幅可能性。芝商所(CME Group)FedWatch工具顯示，週二公布數據指出，美國10月零售銷售溫和成長，進一步強化市場對下個月升息的預期。
Monex USA駐華盛頓交易部門資深總監Juan Perez表示，「目前聯準會似乎非常堅定的準備升息，甚至可能採取更激進的升息方式。」
Perez指出，「這正是目前支撐美元走強的市場信念。」
不過，策略師也警告，美元若要延續升勢，可能需要新的利多催化因素。
Pepperstone研究策略師Dilin Wu表示，「若要推動美元從目前水準進一步顯著走高，市場可能需要開始反映2027年更為激進的升息路徑。」
CME FedWatch工具顯示，交易員預期，12個月後聯準會基準利率將較目前上升約75個基點，來到4.50%至4.75%的區間。投資人也將密切關注紐約聯準銀行總裁威廉斯(John Williams)、聯準會理事巴爾(Michael Barr)，以及明尼阿波利斯聯準銀行總裁卡什卡里(Neel Kashkari)稍晚的談話，以判斷央行下一步政策方向。
美元漲勢已將其他主要貨幣推向數個月來低點。
歐元兌美元下跌0.2%，至1.09735美元，盤中一度觸及2025年4月以來最低。
英鎊兌美元下跌0.3%，至1.3165美元，創一個月來新低。數據顯示，英國10月核心通膨率與前一個月持平，降低市場對英格蘭銀行(BoE)即將升息的預期。
日元大致持平，報159.29日元兌1美元。日本央行(BoJ)總裁植田和男重申，貨幣政策仍有進一步緊縮的必要。日元目前仍接近日本政府今年7月曾進場干預、試圖支撐疲弱日元時的價位。
市場也關注預定於週四在深圳舉行的三方會談，與會者包括美國總統川普、中國國家主席習近平，以及俄羅斯總統普丁(Vladimir Putin)。會談可能涉及俄羅斯對烏克蘭的戰爭、伊朗戰爭，以及貿易、AI與核武等議題。

paras_en: The dollar strengthened on Wednesday (the 18th), reaching a 19‑month high, boosted by hawkish comments from Fed official Christopher Waller and recent economic data, solidifying market expectations of a rate hike next month.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, rose 0.2% to 103.78, the highest since April 2025.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh refused to provide forward guidance, causing investors to rely more on economic data and remarks from other policymakers to gauge the Fed’s next move.

In a CNBC interview, Waller said that if the central bank wants to bring inflation down, it must take more “aggressive action,” including a 0.5‑percentage‑point rate hike at the December meeting or guiding market expectations in the post‑meeting statement to prepare for further hikes.

Last week’s inflation data came in hotter than expected, leading the market to fully price in a 25‑basis‑point Fed hike in December while still seeing a small chance of a 50‑basis‑point increase. CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed that Tuesday’s data, which reported modest growth in U.S. retail sales for October, further reinforced expectations of a rate hike next month.
Juan Perez, senior director of Monex USA’s Washington trading desk, said, “The Fed now appears very resolute in preparing to raise rates, and may even adopt a more aggressive tightening path.”
Perez added, “That is the market belief currently underpinning the dollar’s strength.”
However, strategists warned that for the dollar to keep climbing, a new bullish catalyst may be needed.

Dilin Wu, a strategist at Pepperstone, said, “To push the dollar significantly higher from current levels, the market may need to start pricing in a more aggressive rate‑hike trajectory through 2027.”

CME’s FedWatch tool shows traders expect the Fed’s benchmark rate to be about 75 basis points higher in 12 months, landing in the 4.50%‑4.75% range. Investors will also watch later remarks from New York Fed President John Williams, Fed Governor Michael Barr, and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari to gauge the central bank’s next policy step.
The dollar’s rally has pushed other major currencies toward multi‑month lows.
The euro fell 0.2% against the dollar to $1.09735, briefly touching its lowest level since April 2025.
The pound slipped 0.3% to $1.3165, a one‑month low. Data showed Britain’s core inflation for October held steady month‑over‑month, easing market expectations of an imminent BoE rate hike.

The yen was roughly flat at ¥159.29 per dollar. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated that monetary policy still needs further tightening. The yen remains near the level the Japanese government intervened at in July this year to support the weak currency.

Yuanta Securities noted that international market focus is on two major news items: first, whether Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s departure will disrupt AI chip orders and outlook, fortunately the just‑released earnings were better than expected.

Second, inflation and rate‑hike pressure: with Fed officials continuing hawkish rhetoric, Yuanta Securities believes the probability of a December rate hike is approaching 90%, keeping the US 10‑year Treasury yield above 5%.
